subject.title: Feature: Granular Discord action gates (split actions.messages into read/edit/delete)

question: Should Discord add independently configurable message permissions, and what exact compatibility/default precedence should apply between the existing boolean `actions.messages` shorthand and any per-operation configuration?
rationale: The request adds a public, security-sensitive configuration contract whose defaults determine whether existing Discord deployments retain, gain, or lose destructive capabilities; source-only evidence cannot safely choose that policy.

options.title: Approve one compatible per-operation map
options.body: Keep the boolean shorthand as an all-message-actions setting and add a documented per-operation map with explicit precedence and secure defaults.

options.title: Keep the coarse permission boundary
options.body: Retain the current boolean gate if a single message-action trust boundary is the intended Discord safety model.

options.title: Choose another public permission shape
options.body: Specify separately named action gates or another model before implementation so the plugin API and documentation have one canonical contract.

recommendation.title: Approve one compatible per-operation map
recommendation.body: Keep the boolean shorthand as an all-message-actions setting and add a documented per-operation map with explicit precedence and secure defaults.

likelyOwner.reason: The supplied discussion shows direct prior review of this exact design gap and ongoing interest in the item; no stronger feature-history owner could be verified.
